en: Itivuttaka 16: Ekakanipāta, Second Chapter Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having thus spoken, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, immediately after the Blessed One had departed, the Venerable Ānanda approached the Venerable Sāriputta. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Sāriputta and, having exchanged courteous and amiable words, sat down to one side. Sitting there, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Venerable Sāriputta: "Friend Sāriputta, the Blessed One, having risen from his seat after speaking these words, entered his dwelling. Immediately after the Blessed One had departed, I thought: 'What was the meaning of those words spoken by the Blessed One? "It is wonderful, friend Ānanda! It is marvelous, friend Ānanda! How well this has been stated by the Blessed One: 'One thing, friends, leads to the decline of a noble disciple. And what is that one thing, friend? It is the lack of faith in the Teacher. This, friend, is the one thing that leads to the decline of a noble disciple. "It is wonderful, friend Sāriputta! It is marvelous, friend Sāriputta! How well this has been stated by the Blessed One: 'One thing, friends, leads to the welfare and happiness of a noble disciple for a long time. And what is that one thing, friend? It is faith in the Teacher. This, friend, is the one thing that leads to the welfare and happiness of a noble disciple for a long time. The First Discourse on the Trainee.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu who is a trainee, who has not yet attained his heart's ideal, and who aspires to the unsurpassed security from bondage..."
“Monks, for one who dwells making internal attention a factor, I do not see any other single factor that is so helpful as this:
wise attention. By paying wise attention, monks, a bhikkhu abandons what is unwholesome and develops what is wholesome.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
In this regard, it is said:
For a monk in training, there is no other thing so helpful for the attainment of the supreme goal as the Dhamma.
“A bhikkhu who exerts himself with systematic attention will reach the destruction of suffering.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
